messages:
maya-cs: Heads up — NimbusPay SSO started failing after their IdP metadata refresh. Users get 403 on login. Customer says window ~10:12am PST. Can someone triage?

devin-support: Ticket #INC-9982 linked. Any error ids from our auth logs or a sample SAMLResponse (redact PII)?

maya-cs: Pasting redacted log line we saw: 
`auth: sso callback 403 SAML_ASSERTION_ATTR_MISSING cid=cid-7a3b`
Customer pasted a base64 SAMLResponse; I decoded and saw NameID format change.

devin-support: Yep saw same correlation id in logs: `2026-03-15T17:12:34Z auth ERROR cid=cid-7a3b SAML checks failed: expected NameIDFormat urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress, got urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient`

lee-identity: Can you fetch their current IdP metadata and check AssertionConsumerService bindings and NameIDPolicy? Suspect their rotation replaced metadata that removed POST ACS or changed NameID defaults. Run: 
```
curl -s https://idp.nimbuspay.example/metadata | xmllint --format - | rg "AssertionConsumerService|NameIDPolicy"
```

maya-cs: Ran it. Snippet of metadata: 
```
<AssertionConsumerService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect" Location="https://app.nimbuspay.example/sso/callback" index="0"/>
<NameIDFormat>urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient</NameIDFormat>
```
Our SP config expects POST binding and NameIDFormat=emailAddress.

ashok-sre: Hmm. So metadata now advertises Redirect-only ACS and transient NameID by default. Two paths: 1) Ask Nimbus to restore previous metadata (preferred). 2) Temporary server-side relax checks to accept transient/untyped NameID or use AttributeStatement email if present. Do we see an email attribute in the assertion?

lee-identity: I inspected the decoded assertion — there is no AttributeStatement with email. Customer confirms their IdP team removed attribute release for email during their metadata roll.

maya-cs: Nimbus SSO admin confirmed they accidentally removed the attribute release rule during a config push. They can push a fix but ETA ~2h. Customers are blocked.

ashok-sre: I'll prepare a canary patch to accept transient NameID and attempt to extract email heuristically (if NameID contains @) or accept login and flag for downstream mapping. Low-risk change: fallback path only, gated behind config and audit logs. Any objections? :eyes:

lee-identity: Fine as a short-term mitigation. Add audit events and rate-limit the relax. Also add a toggle per-tenant. We must not widen behavior long-term.

ashok-sre: Plan: deploy canary to 5% on Dedicated and Hosted will follow. Patch summary: 
- Accept SAML NameID of format transient if AttributeStatement has email OR NameID contains '@'
- Emit event: saml.mitigation_applied: true, original_nameid_format, tenant_id
- Fail closed if no email found after heuristics

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started: service=auth-saml, env=prod, canary=5%, initiated_by=ashok-sre

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary healthy after 6m — no regressions, latency + error rates within baseline.

devin-support: After canary we saw a handful of logins succeed for Nimbus users. Still waiting on IdP to restore email attribute.

lee-identity: Also validated ACS binding: our SP accepts POST and Redirect, but our strict config preferred POST. I updated SP config to accept Redirect temporarily for that tenant only (toggle set). Documenting steps to revert when IdP fixes metadata.

maya-cs: Customer updated — they will push corrected metadata within 90 minutes. They asked for our rollback steps when they confirm.

ashok-sre: Rollback notes: revert tenant toggle, remove heuristic acceptance, remove audit flag. I'll create a revert PR and link it to the ticket.

devin-support: Noted. I've updated ticket INC-9982 with mitigation steps and status. Customer notified.

lee-identity: I'll add a KB article: "How to validate SAML IdP metadata for Redwood SP compatibility" with commands to check ACS binding and NameID formats and a checklist for attribute release.

maya-cs: Thanks all. Marking this thread to follow until Nimbus confirms metadata push. Will @oncall if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
